problem: Saying the camera 'looks along the cylinder axis' hides the folding: the light travels down the axis through the crown window, then the 45° mirror turns it out sideways, so the camera itself sits beside the engine looking horizontally.
fix: The Bowditch extended piston has a window in the crown and a 45° mirror below it in the piston extension. The line of sight passes down the cylinder axis through the window and the mirror folds it out sideways to a camera mounted beside the engine.

problem: The sentence 'it fires only a few cycles, so cycle-to-cycle variation is large' gives the wrong cause. Firing few cycles makes the variation hard to measure; the variation itself comes from the low compression ratio, non-production chamber and uneven wall temperatures.
fix: It fires only a few cycles before fouling stops the run, so the cycle-to-cycle scatter is poorly sampled; the simplified chamber and different wall conditions also tend to make that scatter larger than in a production engine.

problem: 532 nm is not the natural output of Nd:YAG; it is the frequency-doubled second harmonic. A student may quote 532 nm as the fundamental wavelength.
fix: Nd:YAG, frequency-doubled to 532 nm (the fundamental is 1064 nm), excimer such as XeCl at 308 nm, and tunable dye lasers.

problem: LDA measures velocity at one point; swirl or tumble is obtained only by traversing the measurement volume across the cylinder, which the sentence does not say.
fix: LDA measures the velocity at a single point from the Doppler shift of particles crossing the fringes; traversing that point across the cylinder builds up the swirl or tumble profile.
